indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of the verb
limber means supple, able to bend easily

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: start by growing a plant that bends easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber is any plant that grows upward by clinging to walls, trellises or other supports.

clue.text: Wolf's retiring up to a point

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: a retiring person is shy
taken as written
east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A wolf is said to be shy only to a certain degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a small North American member of the dog family, often called the prairie wolf.

blocks.note: the word combine holds a bin inside its other letters, so describe where that receptacle sits

explanation.surface: A farmer wants a hopper resembling a harvester's to collect the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: A combine is a harvesting machine, but here it is the word: COMBINE is BIN inside COME, so its receptacle sits IN COME.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money received regularly, from work or investments, the same as revenue or earnings.

clue.text: Hold up by holding forth a flower

blocks.note: first meaning: to detain someone by talking at them
second meaning: a bloom worn in a lapel slit

explanation.surface: Someone is delayed by a speaker presenting a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to waylay someone in conversation; as a noun, a single bloom pinned to a jacket lapel.

blocks.note: first meaning: to tangle or complicate
second meaning: the French composer of Boléro, one who writes scores

explanation.surface: Muddle the person keeping count in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to entangle threads, and Maurice Ravel was a composer who wrote orchestral music.

clue.text: Strange isle is a part of Europe

indicators.note: something strange is odd and out of its usual form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all three words are used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A traveller remarks that an odd island belongs to Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historical region of central Europe, now mostly within Poland with smaller Czech and German portions.

clue.text: Blade with large amount of flavour?

blocks.note: a spear, or a blade of grass or leaf shoot
a mint is a huge sum of money

explanation.surface: A knife and a big helping make a tasty dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the plant is a flavouring rather than a flavour itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a herb whose oil is used to give chewing gum and toothpaste their taste.

indicators.note: to house something is to contain it, so the letters lie inside the words

blocks.note: across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone manages venues staging old-style opera.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy, bounding strides.

clue.text: End of game on board being with Jack?

blocks.note: on board means aboard a ship
checkmate ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: Checkmate on the chessboard, with someone called Jack watching.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or Jack tar, is an old name for a sailor, so a being with him is a fellow crew member.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a fellow sailor serving aboard the same vessel, a companion at sea.

clue.text: Gold also coats gear lifting aircraft

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the word so it reads from bottom to top
to coat something is to cover it all round, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
too means also
rig is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: Gold plating covers the machinery that lifts an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: An autogiro is an early rotorcraft with an unpowered rotor for lift and a propeller for thrust.

clue.text: Your old backer keeps tab for main racer

indicators.note: a backer here is a word written back to front, read from its end
to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: thy is the archaic form of your
a tab is an account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned sponsor picks up the bill for a racing entrant.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is a poetic word for the open sea, so a main racer is a boat built for racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing vessel often used in sea races, hence a racer on the ocean.

blocks.note: surface reading: a pimple or mark leading on to another one
setter's reading: a place from which to spot, that is to see, things

explanation.walkthrough: The first spot is a noun meaning a location, the second a verb meaning to catch sight of.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewpoint is a vantage place chosen for looking out over scenery, so a location for seeing.

blocks.note: surface reading: the capers of someone called Jerry
setter's reading: the cartoon mouse Jerry spends his time making a fool of the cat Tom

explanation.walkthrough: Tom and Jerry is the cartoon in which the mouse endlessly outwits the cat, so his antics are literally fooling Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means silly, playful behaviour or clowning, which describes cartoon slapstick well.

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
MS is manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An instruction to compose an essay on environmental pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Smog is a dense haze of smoke and fog, a common form of urban air contamination.

clue.text: Defamation gets student sent down for flier

indicators.note: a student sent down is expelled; here the letter is taken out and placed lower in the word

blocks.note: slandering is speaking defamation
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student accused of libel is expelled and flies home.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'sent down' moves the L further down the word, from second place to after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanderling is a small grey and white wading bird that runs along beaches, so a bird.

clue.text: Home-life to be outside from now on

indicators.note: one piece is to stand outside, wrapping round the other

blocks.note: the life to come after death
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Domestic life is to be lived out of doors from now on.
explanation.walkthrough: The afterlife is the hereafter; 'home' goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereinafter is a legal word meaning in the following part of this document, thus from this point forward.

indicators.note: to be inveigled is to be coaxed and manipulated, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: both words supply letters

explanation.surface: Someone was coaxed or lured into something covertly.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure or little known, knowledge hidden from most people.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to check is to stop
to man a boat is to crew it

explanation.surface: A man wearing a chequered hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' and 'check' look like nouns but are verbs: crew and stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwtop is a lid that twists on to close a bottle or jar, so a type of cap.

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
one who catches animals with a rope or lasso

explanation.surface: A sinister child catcher is behaving indecently.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Child Catcher of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang, but the phrase splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper conduct breaks the standards of decency, the same as being indecorous or unbecoming.

clue.text: Fell into line without whip being involved

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to fall into line is to obey
the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip

explanation.surface: Someone toed the line only because no whip was used on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something involved has many interlocking parts, the same sense as intricate or convoluted.

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the abbreviation for yard
a republic in South America

explanation.surface: A lizard sits a yard away from the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, a plant-eating reptile with a spiny crest.

indicators.note: a bit is only a portion of the words, so the letters lie within them

blocks.note: across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A shared bequest turns out to be rather stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy, but it is the verb meaning to have in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to plan or have a purpose, so to mean to do something.

indicators.note: topping and tailing cuts off both ends, the first letter and the last

blocks.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A nobleman has very nearly been beheaded and docked.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking above viscount and below marquess, so an aristocrat.

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: all three words supply letters

explanation.surface: A hip-hop track sits beside a wild bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild flower' reads as one phrase, but 'wild' acts on the words before it and 'flower' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, Antirrhinum, is a garden plant whose blooms open like a mouth when squeezed.

clue.text: Tinted leaf with phosphorus and other things

blocks.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
et al., Latin for and others

explanation.surface: A coloured leaf treated with phosphorus and various extras.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the coloured leaf-like segments forming the corolla of a bloom.

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to boast is to brag

explanation.surface: Fine clothes worth showing off about.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing or dress, especially distinctive attire.

blocks.note: surface reading: someone looking smart and slim, as in cutting a fine figure
setter's reading: a gardener who clips hedges into neat shapes such as birds or animals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut a figure' is an idiom for making an impression; here the cutting is literal shears on a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: This craftsman practises the art of shaping bushes and hedges into ornamental forms.

clue.text: Proclaim a genuine case for representation

indicators.note: the words act as a case, a container holding the letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A lawyer declares a real argument for someone to be represented.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness, a picture or statue that depicts something.

blocks.note: par is the standard or normal level
fit in the sense of capable

explanation.surface: A family member who is ordinarily in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a family member, but here it means a story that is related, or told.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale, and a relation can mean a narrative or account.

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the following pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: split as over plus haul; to haul is to drag
a gal is a girl

explanation.surface: An instruction to overtake a woman who is dawdling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhaul' looks like one word meaning to overtake; split it as 'over' plus 'haul'.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard falls behind others, the same as a dawdler or someone moving too slowly.
